summary:
TerraTwin is an interactive geospatial platform to discover and rank the closest planetary analogs to the Earth for surface exploration on the Moon and Mars.

We proposed a dual-module architecture with offline preprocessing of NASA datasets (MOLA, THEMIS, Diviner, and MODIS) to address the problem of locating accurate terrestrial testing sites. The Rover Mobility engine computes model-based terrain similarity scores to rank Earth candidates and selected planetary targets in an objective manner. The Thermal Testing dashboard simultaneously presents processed environmental observations: 384 lunar Diviner products and 20 Mars targets, enabling investigators to investigate data provenance and thermal extremes.

This matters because testing multi-billion dollar hardware in inaccurate Earth environments is a catastrophic risk. TerraTwin replaces superficial visual comparisons with a transparent, multi-variable data pipeline, allowing mission planners to confidently select terrestrial testing sites based on hard physical and thermal evidence.
details:
1. What it does and how it works

TerraTwin is a data fusion platform that finds and ranks the closest physical Earth analogs for any given location on Mars and the Moon.

The workflow is driven by two different modules:

Rover Mobility (Terrain Similarity): User selects a planetary target (e.g., Hadley Rille or Mare Tranquillitatis Pit). TerraTwin retrieves pre-processed planetary terrain data and compares them against global Earth candidate grids. The engine calculates a model-derived terrain similarity percentage based on physical feature vectors (e.g., mean slope, roughness, elevation variability, and curvature) and objectively ranks Earth candidates.

Thermal Testing (Environmental Evidence) Yet another interactive dashboard for thermal extremes and provenance of data. Earth MODIS data, THEMIS observations of Mars (20 integrated targets), and 384 processed lunar Diviner polar archive products are available for inspection by researchers.

1. Expected Impact and Benefits

Testing multi-billion dollar planetary hardware in the wrong terrestrial environment is a catastrophic and expensive gamble. Historically, analog selection has depended on established sites (e.g. the Atacama Desert or Haughton Crater) based on visual or geological assumptions.

TerraTwin’s impact is that it replaces subjective, pre-selected analog testing with a global, multi-variable data pipeline. Earth is scanned in 5km x 5km tiles to reveal new test grounds that meet accurate planetary engineering constraints. The benefit to mission planners is an explicit, measurable basis for site selection, minimizing the risk of rover mobility failures or thermal hardware degradation.

3. Tools, Languages and Architecture

To make the application highly responsive and scientifically rigorous, our team of five designed a decoupled data pipeline:

Scientific data sources: Google Earth Engine (GEE), NASA MODIS, MOLA, THEMIS, Diviner and USGS SRTM elevation data.

Data Pipeline & Backend: For offline geospatial preprocessing, QA diagnostics, and creating harmonized CSV/JSON datasets (e.g. earth_thermal.csv), we used Python. The backend is served with FastAPI server using Uvicorn and Pydantic.

Frontend & Visualization The UI is built with React, TypeScript and Vite, plots complex thermal data with Recharts and is statically deployed with Vercel.

4. How the Project is Creative

Our creativity lies in scientific restraint and architectural design.

Rather than forcing a single "magic number" that combines terrain and thermal data, we deliberately separated the Rover Mobility ranking from the Thermal Testing module. We recognized that Earth thermal observations are not yet scientifically validated for cross-planet thermal scoring. Presenting them as separate evidence channels prevents researchers from relying on flawed, artificially fused data.

Additionally, we moved the massive computational burden of processing satellite archives entirely offline. Instead of making live API calls that would crash during a demo, TerraTwin serves prepared GeoJSONs to a static frontend, ensuring instant load times and passing 101 automated frontend tests.


5. Factors Our Team Considered

  • Scientific Integrity: We explicitly define our similarity percentage as a model-derived terrain comparison index, not a guarantee of a rover's probability of success.
  • Data Gaps: When handling the 719 valid site-season bins from the lunar Diviner data, we programmed the UI to preserve missing measurements as explicit gaps rather than interpolating or guessing values, preserving the raw truth of the data.
  • End-User Constraints: We optimized the UI for researchers and hackathon judges, ensuring that complex planetary data can be navigated without downloading gigabytes of raw satellite imagery, allowing it to run smoothly even on throttled mobile networks.
